name: fix_ruby_each_instead_of_map
description: Fixes a Ruby method that uses `each` (returning the receiver) where it must `map` to build a transformed array
prompts: Doubler#doubled in lib/doubler.rb should return a NEW array with every element doubled, preserving order. It uses `nums.each { |n| n * 2 }`, but Enumerable#each returns the original array (the block's value is discarded), so the numbers are never doubled. Fix it to return the doubled array (use map). Keep the class and method signature.

setup_files.lib/doubler.rb:
module App
  class Doubler
    # Return a NEW array with every element doubled, in the same order.
    # BUG: `each` runs the block for its side effects and returns the
    # ORIGINAL array, so the elements are never actually doubled.
    def doubled(nums)
      nums.each { |n| n * 2 }
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.test/doubler_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/doubler"

class DoublerHiddenTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_doubles_each_element
    assert_equal [2, 4, 6], App::Doubler.new.doubled([1, 2, 3])
  end

  def test_preserves_order
    assert_equal [20, 4], App::Doubler.new.doubled([10, 2])
  end

  def test_empty
    assert_equal [], App::Doubler.new.doubled([])
  end
end

reference_solution.lib/doubler.rb:
module App
  class Doubler
    # Return a NEW array with every element doubled, in the same order.
    def doubled(nums)
      nums.map { |n| n * 2 }
    end
  end
end
